title: Northbeam Returns and Restocking: How Many Authorisations One Profile May Carry
content:
**The rule.** A customer may have several Northbeam Returns and Restocking authorisations open at once, and the number on one profile is not limited in itself. A second authorisation is never raised on an order line that already carries one standing in requested, authorized, in transit, received or inspected. Where a line was returned in part and the customer wants to return more of it, a fresh authorisation is raised for the further units, and the units already settled are not counted again. A profile may not have more authorisations open at one time than the schedule's concurrent limit allows, counted across every schedule; where the limit is reached the customer settles or withdraws one before another is raised. The concurrent limit is read from the count of authorisations standing open on the profile at the moment the new authorisation is raised.

**One live authorisation per order line.** The condition is tested against the return authorisation records themselves and not against what the customer says is outstanding, and it is tested before the new authorisation is raised. The authorisations compared are those matched to the same order line as the one now being raised. An authorisation counts as already standing on that line while its status is requested, authorized, in transit, received or inspected; an authorisation that has settled, been denied or been withdrawn does not. Where a further authorisation is properly raised on the same line it is a separate record, told apart from the earlier one by the day the return was asked for and by the units it covers.

**What "standing open" counts for the concurrent limit.** The same five statuses — requested, authorized, in transit, received and inspected — are the ones counted, and the count is taken across every schedule the profile holds rather than within one schedule. The figure it is compared with is the concurrent limit of the schedule the new line falls under.

**Two worked situations, on hypothetical facts.**

*A profile carrying two authorisations, both inspected, on a schedule whose concurrent limit is three.* Both count as standing open, the count is two, and a third authorisation may be raised.

*A profile carrying one authorisation on the order line the customer now wants to return, that authorisation standing received.* No second authorisation is raised on that line, whatever the concurrent limit allows, because the line already carries one standing in one of the five statuses.

*A line of four units, two of them already returned and settled.* A fresh authorisation is raised for the further units, and the two already settled are not counted again in it.
